title: The Water Cycle
description: How water moves between the sea, the sky and the land — reading, diagram, narration and six questions.

image.caption: The water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection.

paragraphs: The water on Earth is always moving. The same water has been used again and again for millions of years. This journey is called the water cycle.
First, the Sun heats water in seas, rivers and lakes. Some of the water turns into an invisible gas called water vapour and rises into the air. This is called evaporation.

sections.heading: From the sky to the land
paragraphs: High in the sky the air is cold. The water vapour cools down and changes back into tiny drops of water. The drops join together to make clouds. This is called condensation.
When the drops become too heavy, they fall to the ground as rain, snow or hail. This is called precipitation.
The water collects in rivers, lakes and under the ground, and much of it flows back to the sea. Then the cycle starts again.
